{"id":"COR-2310","uuid":"0370fb5d-4222-4426-9f4f-b1b64e7dc564","title":"Brain: measure what brief's history arm uniquely surfaced; close distill coverage gaps","description":"**Repo:** entireio/entire-brain · **Phase C of the memories-only retrieval decision** (see <issue id="e540d772-0613-4636-a0e3-137441d4668b" label="COR-2307" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2307/brain-brief-precedent-section-from-fact-provenance-anchors-not-history" />)

## Why

Distill is lossy by design: \~263k transcript-derived history records collapse into \~2.8k facts. With history search leaving brief's default path (<issue id="42fefac0-46c9-4341-8538-f9c3a4b3958b" label="COR-2308" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2308/brain-remove-history-search-and-the-raw-scan-from-briefs-default-path" />), anything only the history arm could surface becomes invisible to the default flow. Each such gap is now a distill bug, not a reason to restore a second search system.

## Work

1. **Measure:** replay a representative set of recent brief tasks (the repo's own session history is the corpus) on a build with the old history arm and a memories-only build. Diff the history/precedent sections. Classify every hit the old arm had that the new flow lacks: (a) content also present in a fact the ranking missed → ranking bug (file against the ranking issue), (b) content never distilled → coverage gap, (c) noise (derived-index junk, duplicate copies) → no action.
2. **Decide on mention-grade facts:** for class (b), evaluate a cheap fact kind recording "session X touched identifier/file Y" with locus and anchors, extracted without an extra LLM pass if possible. It must carry its own distill budget — the store at \~2.8k facts is healthy, and mention bloat would degrade recall precision. Rejecting mention-facts and accepting the gap explicitly is a valid outcome; record either decision in Brain with rationale.

## Acceptance

* A written classification of the diff (counts per class, examples).
* Either a mention-grade fact design agreed and filed for implementation, or a recorded decision to accept the gap.","priority":{"value":0,"name":"No priority"},"url":"https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2310/brain-measure-what-briefs-history-arm-uniquely-surfaced-close-distill","gitBranchName":"evis/cor-2310-brain-measure-what-briefs-history-arm-uniquely","createdAt":"2026-11-09T04:57:43.047Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-10T04:59:15.901Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":"2026-11-10T04:59:15.885Z","startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Done","statusType":"completed","labels":[],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Evis Drenova","createdById":"bd1c458e-3bb3-4d0c-8ad7-e36f19afc156","assignee":"Evis Drenova","assigneeId":"bd1c458e-3bb3-4d0c-8ad7-e36f19afc156","team":"Core","teamId":"894690b6-2173-4cbe-abd3-6e7ea5ff5bb9"}

Retrieval (query takes --json/--format json|cli/--limit/-n/--branch,
get/multi-get take --json/--format json|cli/--branch):
  entire brain query "<query>" --json       # hybrid (lexical+vector, RRF) — the default
  entire brain query --keyword "<query>" --json      # lexical keyword over memories + history + docs (BM25 for history/docs)
  entire brain query --semantic "<query>" --json     # vector/semantic over memories + docs (+ history/conversation with a Gemma-class embedder)
  entire brain get <id> --json              # fetch one item by id (fact:… | history:… | doc:…)
  entire brain multi-get <id>... --json     # fetch several by id

Small top-level surface:
  entire brain status [repo] --json         # sources, memories+verification, semantic coverage/freshness/blind spots, live state
  entire brain status --fail-on release     # CI gate: nonzero when freshness is not ok or blind spots exist (also: unsafe, degraded, blind-spots)
  entire brain overview [repo] --json
  entire brain brief "<task>" --json
  entire brain show <id> --json
  entire brain agent-guide
  entire brain path [repo]

Durable memories (curated, provenance-anchored repo knowledge):
  entire brain distill --dry-run --json
  entire brain recall "<query>" [--scope local|cross-cutting] [--expand] --json
  entire brain remember "<memory>" [--path category.sub.type] --json
  entire brain verify [<memory-id | query>] --json
  entire brain memories tree [--path <prefix>] [--depth N]
  entire brain memories retract <memory-id> --json
  entire brain inspect blame <memory-id> --json # source anchors a memory was derived from

Specialist tools (symbol graph + regression analysis — what the verbs can't do):
  entire brain inspect code "<query>" --json        # find a symbol in the graph
  entire brain inspect search-graph "<query>" --json
  entire brain inspect query-graph "type:CALLS <query>" --json
  entire brain inspect graph-ui semantic-graph.html
  entire brain inspect snippet <symbol-or-id> --json
  entire brain inspect trace-path <from-symbol> <to-symbol> --json
  entire brain inspect dead-code --json
  entire brain inspect ingest-traces <json-or-ndjson-file> --json
  entire brain inspect context <symbol-or-id> --json
  entire brain inspect impact <symbol-or-file> --json
  entire brain inspect changes --json
  entire brain inspect tests "<query>" --json
  entire brain inspect boundaries --kind route|tool|workflow --json
  entire brain inspect regressions "<query>" --location-only [--include-deletions] --json

Available Commands:
  files        Write durable memories out as plain Markdown files you can grep, read and diff
  gc           Prune retracted and old superseded memories; report orphans
  global       List memories recorded globally rather than for one repository
  import       Import durable memories from another memory tool's export
  map          Render the synthesized memory outline (summaries + structure) with progressive disclosure
  outline      Generate the synthesized hierarchical memory outline (agent rollup summaries)
  retract      Mark a memory as retracted (no longer true); pruned later by gc
  status       Summarize durable memory readiness without refreshing or writing
  storage      Inspect or migrate memory storage
  sync         Sync this branch's local memories with the team's hosted memory set
  tree         Show memories as a navigable hierarchy with progressive disclosure
  vitality     Show serve receipts per memory (which memories the read surfaces actually emitted)

Flags:
	var syncOpts factsSyncOptions
	cmd := &cobra.Command{
		Use:   "sync",
		Short: "Sync this branch's local memories with the team's hosted memory set",
		Long: `sync exchanges this branch's local memories with the team's hosted memory set
over the per-fact wire: push this branch's memories, pull the team's delta feed.
It is the same exchange the background sync runs, except failures fail the
command instead of degrading silently.

Memory sync is hosted-only. The default target is the connected binding
('` + base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "connect") + `'); on an unconnected repo a plain sync fails and
memories stay local. The local-gitmeta backend was removed (COR-2236):
--memories-backend accepts only "http", and the explicit target resolves
flag > env > connected binding (--api-url/ENTIRE_API_URL,
--repo-id/ENTIRE_REPO_ID, --token/ENTIRE_API_TOKEN; on a connected repo the
binding supplies the target and the token is minted automatically).

ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS (or its deprecated alias ENTIRE_BRAIN_LOCAL_ONLY)
suppresses all hosted sync regardless of defaults and flags.`,
		Args: cobra.NoArgs,
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			return runFactsSync(cmd, opts, syncOpts)
		},
	}
	cmd.Flags().StringVar(&syncOpts.branch, "branch", "", "Branch to sync (default: current branch)")

{"id":"COR-2313","title":"Brain: recall loads the fact store up to three times per query","description":"**Repo:** entireio/entire-brain · From the 2026-11-06 retrieval audit (survey at main c1d42ec0 — verify line refs against current main).

## Problem

One `recall` parses the full fact store up to three times: `factstore.Load` (`internal/cli/command/facts/facts_read_cmd.go:103`), `factstore.InspectBrain` for the integrity check (`:139`, re-loads via `integrity.go:298`), and `EmptyResultBlindSpot` on empty results (`:221`, `:243`, loads again in `blind_spot.go`). It also spawns \~4 git subprocesses, including `git rev-parse HEAD` for the vitality receipt — a locked write that by design never affects ranking (`facts_vitality.go:27`).

Post-migration the store is one 3.4 MB `store.json` (\~2.8k facts) and recall measures \~0.27s, so this is structural, not urgent — the cost returns as the corpus grows.

## Change

* Load once; pass the loaded records to the integrity check and the blind-spot explainer. The call sites live behind the `facts.Config`/`Deps` seams, so this is threading a value.
* Decide the receipt write: drop it, batch it, or make it feed ranking (<issue id="3f94fa5e-4145-45b0-b9b8-c657a3b766b5" label="COR-2311" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2311/brain-recall-ranking-quality-collapse-related-ids-pairs-recency-prior" /> territory). Today it is cost with no benefit.
* Out of scope: a persisted BM25 postings sidecar — only if measurement shows tokenization dominating at real corpus sizes.

## Acceptance

One store parse per recall; existing recall tests green."}

+// LoadWithIntegrity is Load plus the integrity report computed from the same
+// parse, so a read surface needs one pass over the store instead of one per
+// concern (COR-2313). The report matches InspectBrain: a manifest that will
+// not load or declares no fact source reads as healthy.
+func LoadWithIntegrity(brainDir string) ([]factmerge.Record, Integrity, error) {
+  combined, err := loadCombined(brainDir)
+  if err != nil {
+    return nil, Integrity{}, err
+  records := combined.sorted()
+  manifest, merr := bmanifest.Load(brainDir)
+  if merr != nil || manifest == nil || manifest.Sources == nil {
+    return records, Integrity{}, nil
+  return records, inspectCombined(manifest.Sources.Facts, combined), nil
// Write replaces the flat store with exactly these records. Callers hold the
// brain write lock over their load-mutate-write; the store lock additionally
// serializes snapshot commits.

While the suites run: the work so far on COR-2313 —

- `factstore.LoadWithIntegrity` returns records plus the integrity report from one `loadCombined` parse; `Inspect` now delegates to the extracted `inspectCombined`.
- Recall uses it: one store parse instead of two, and the blind-spot explainer receives the already-computed report instead of parsing a third time (the seam takes `nil` from query/retrieve callers, whose behavior is unchanged).
- Receipt decision: **keep** — vitality receipts are the documented Phase 1 of the lifecycle ledger whose Phase 3 decay is the planned ranking feed, and the write is best-effort/never-fails by contract. Will record on the issue.
- New test pins the single-parse contract against `Load` + `InspectBrain` on healthy and lossy stores.

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
perf(recall): one store parse per query

recall parsed the full memory store up to three times: factstore.Load for
the records, InspectBrain for the integrity warning (a second loadCombined
behind the same manifest), and the empty-result blind-spot note (a third,
via factstore.Inspect). Post-migration that is one 3.4 MB store.json, so
this was structural rather than slow, but the cost returns as the corpus
grows.

factstore.LoadWithIntegrity returns the records and the integrity report
from one parse (Inspect's post-load body is extracted as
inspectCombined). recall threads its report into the blind-spot explainer,
whose seam now takes an optional precomputed report; query/retrieve pass
nil and keep their behavior.

The vitality serve receipt stays: it is Phase 1 of the lifecycle ledger
(docs/vitality_receipts.md) whose Phase 3 decay is the planned ranking
input, and the write is best-effort/never-fails by contract. Decision
recorded on COR-2313.

COR-2313

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git push -q -u origin evisdren/cor-2313-single-store-load 2>&1 | tail -1; gh pr create --base main --title "perf(recall): one store parse per query (COR-2313)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Why

One `recall` parsed the full memory store up to three times: `factstore.Load` for the records, `factstore.InspectBrain` for the integrity warning (a second `loadCombined`), and the empty-result blind-spot note (a third, via `factstore.Inspect`). At today's 3.4 MB flat store this is ~0.27s and structural rather than painful; the cost scales with the corpus. Linear: COR-2313.

## What changed

- `factstore.LoadWithIntegrity(brainDir)` returns the records and the integrity report from one parse. `Inspect`'s post-load body is extracted as `inspectCombined`; `Inspect`/`InspectBrain` behavior is unchanged.
- `recall` uses it and threads the report into the empty-result blind-spot explainer. The explainer's seam (`Deps.EmptyResultBlindSpot`) now takes an optional precomputed `*factstore.Integrity`; `nil` means "compute it yourself", which is what query/retrieve/search still pass — their parse count is COR-2314/scope-adjacent, untouched here.
- The integrity check's semantics are pinned by `TestLoadWithIntegrityMatchesSeparateCalls`: one call equals `Load` + `InspectBrain` on a healthy store and after a lost fact.

## Receipt decision (ticket bullet 2)

The vitality serve receipt (and its `git rev-parse HEAD`) stays. It is Phase 1 of the lifecycle ledger (`docs/vitality_receipts.md`): receipts are the evidence for the Phase 2 outcome join and Phase 3 decay — the "make it feed ranking" path, which is COR-2311-adjacent territory. The write is best-effort and never fails the read surface by contract. Dropping it would orphan `memories vitality` and the documented plan to save one cheap subprocess.

## Validation

`./internal/cli`, `./internal/cli/command/...`, `./internal/cli/internal/factstore` suites pass; `gofmt -s`/`go vet` clean. Acceptance: one store parse per recall (two of three sites eliminated; the remaining parse is the one that loads the records).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -1

Today it is cost with no benefit.
* Out of scope: a persisted BM25 postings sidecar — only if measurement shows tokenization dominating at real corpus sizes.

One `recall` parses the full fact store up to three times: `factstore.Load` (`internal/cli/command/facts/facts_read_cmd.go:103`), `factstore.InspectBrain` for the integrity check (`:139`, re-loads via `integrity.go:298`), and `EmptyResultBlindSpot` on empty results (`:221`, `:243`, loads again in `blind_spot.go`). It also spawns \~4 git subprocesses, including `git rev-parse HEAD` for the vitality receipt — a locked write that by design never affects ranking (`facts_vitality.go:27`).

Post-migration the store is one 3.4 MB `store.json` (\~2.8k facts) and recall measures \~0.27s, so this is structural, not urgent — the cost returns as the corpus grows.

## Change

* Load once; pass the loaded records to the integrity check and the blind-spot explainer. The call sites live behind the `facts.Config`/`Deps` seams, so this is threading a value.
* Decide the receipt write: drop it, batch it, or make it feed ranking (<issue id="3f94fa5e-4145-45b0-b9b8-c657a3b766b5" label="COR-2311" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2311/brain-recall-ranking-quality-collapse-related-ids-pairs-recency-prior" /> territory). Today it is cost with no benefit.
* Out of scope: a persisted BM25 postings sidecar — only if measurement shows tokenization dominating at real corpus sizes.

## Acceptance

{"id":"COR-2315","title":"Brain: seed staleness warning is permanent noise for shared multi-worktree brains","status":"Backlog","attachments":[],"description":"**Repo:** entireio/entire-brain

## Problem

One brain is keyed by the origin remote (`env.go` resolves via `git remote get-url origin`) and shared by every worktree of the repo. The seed counts as fresh only when its commit equals HEAD (`refresh.go:1039-1058`; status axis at `agent_surface.go:4713`). With several Conductor worktrees on different branches, at most one can ever match — every other worktree sees "seed is stale; run refresh" forever, and running refresh just moves the noise to a different worktree.

## Change

Make the freshness check worktree-aware: treat the seed as fresh when its commit is an ancestor of HEAD within a small bound (or HEAD an ancestor of it), and say "built from <sha>, N commits behind" instead of stale/unsafe. +// seedFreshDriftBound is how much one-sided drift between the seed commit and
+// this worktree's HEAD still reads as fresh. One brain is shared by every

+// ever satisfy seed == HEAD; strict equality made the stale warning the
+// PERMANENT state of every other worktree (COR-2315). A worktree a few dozen
+// commits off the seed deserves a detail line, not a warning; hundreds of
+// commits is a genuinely old seed and still warns.
+const seedFreshDriftBound = 50

+// how far each side is from their merge base, which separates near-ancestor
+// drift (ok, with a built-from detail) from real distance or divergence
+// (stale). A comparison that cannot run keeps the stale verdict: an unreadable
+// history must not read as fresh.
+func seedCommitDriftAxis(ctx context.Context, runner CommandRunner, repoDir, seedCommit, head string) staleAxis {
+  refresh := clibase.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "refresh") + " --agent none"
+  stale := staleAxis{State: "stale", Detail: "repository context and docs are based on an older commit; run " + refresh, Current: head, Indexed: seedCommit}
+  counts, err := clibase.GitScalar(ctx, runner, repoDir, "rev-list", "--count", "--left-right", seedCommit+"..."+head)
+  if err != nil {
+    return stale
+  var seedOnly, headOnly int
+  if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(strings.TrimSpace(counts), "%d %d", &seedOnly, &headOnly); err != nil {
+    return stale
+  switch {
+  case seedOnly > 0 && headOnly > 0:
+    stale.Detail = fmt.Sprintf("repository context and docs were built from %s, which diverged from HEAD (%d and %d commits from their merge base); run %s", seedCommit, seedOnly, headOnly, refresh)
+    return stale
+  case headOnly > seedFreshDriftBound || seedOnly > seedFreshDriftBound:
+    stale.Detail = fmt.Sprintf("repository context and docs were built from %s, %d commits from HEAD; run %s", seedCommit, max(seedOnly, headOnly), refresh)
+    return stale
+  case headOnly > 0:
+    return staleAxis{State: "ok", Detail: fmt.Sprintf("repository context and docs were built from %s, %d commit(s) behind HEAD", seedCommit, headOnly), Current: head, Indexed: seedCommit}
+  default:
+    // The seed is ahead: another worktree refreshed on a newer commit and
+    // this one's HEAD is its ancestor.
